what: A system alarm: a failure that could not escalate anywhere else, held by the trouble lane until a recipient says the change was made.
why: A trouble carries the same fields as a development ticket (node_class, schema_version, workflow_and_state) so one parser and one inspector read both, but its path is its own: it is born red when raised and turns green when cleared (Akien, open-178c9f4b537c: 'it's born red and becomes green when cleared'). Its liveness is its location, top of the store or cleared/ (ticket 4ddc9df3369e), and the cursor mirrors that location.

v1.why: Two states. A raise writes [OPEN] at the top of the store; a clear moves the file into cleared/ and writes [CLEARED]; a recurrence moves it back and writes [OPEN] again.

prove_gate: the clear itself: a recipient's what_changed, recorded through the trouble device's door (cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py).
extra_gates: none — a trouble is a logging artifact and ages out of ~/.cairn/logs on the 30-day sweep.
kicks_back_on: a recurrence after a clear: the file returns to the top with prior_attempts incremented and the clear that did not hold still on cleared_by.
provenance: defined 2026-10-12 under ticket 4ddc9df3369e, on Akien's answer to open-178c9f4b537c.
